digest.component_or_area: overlap judge stage-2, prompt caching layer
propositions: The overlap judge re-sends the query ticket digest verbatim in the user message across all batch calls (12 of 12 measured), paying full token cost each time, when the digest is invariant across the batch and could sit in the cacheable system prefix.

Hoisting the shared query digest from the volatile user message into the system prompt makes it part of the cache-eligible prefix, enabling writes on the first call and cheap reads on the remaining N-1 calls per batch.

The measured cache floor for claude-sonnet-4-6 is 1024 tokens, not the 4096 documented for Opus; the hoisted prefix reaches only 846 tokens on real digests, landing below the threshold and yielding zero cache reads/writes while adding +936 tokens (+5.8%) regression via the orientation paragraph.
Precision is preserved under the hoist: all 12 ordered-pair verdicts (relation, shared_artifact, confidence) remain identical between baseline and hoisted implementations on the measured corpus.

The sequential judge loop (plain for-loop, no parallelization) naturally sequences the first call to warm the prefix before remaining calls read it; parallelizing without a completed warm-up call first would degrade cost by turning 1 cache write into N premium writes.
